newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts reverse early gains,end down.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts reverse early gains,end down.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices ended lower after giving back early gains, with Venezuelan Bradys suffering the biggest losses amid concerns the country's fundamentals are beginning to worsen, emerging market sources said.
"I think there is a shift in the outlook for Venezuela. The whole shine is coming off the Venezuelan story," said Tulio Vera, managing director at Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
At 1645 EST/2145 GMT, Venezuelan DCBs were 3-1/8 lower at 84-5/8 bid and the country's par bonds were two percentage points weaker at 72-1/8 bid.
Vera of Bear Stearns said the selloff in Venezuela is consistent with the fundamental picture.
He said lower oil prices, stagnation in the reform process, higher wages and increased volatility in the exchange rate have all added to a worsening scenario for Venezuela.

"The window of opportunity, which we had at the end of the second half of last year to get some of the reforms through is beginning to look narrower and narrower because next year there is the presidential election," Vera added.
In the broader market, sources said Brady prices started to come off late in the day in line with U.S. Treasuries.
Market nervousness ahead of testimony Wednesday by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan and Friday's U.S. employment figures also weighed on the market.
Concerns of a hike in U.S. interest rates at the next FOMC meeting at the end of March added to the market jitters.
"It's a very nervous market. I think it's now up to the market to find a new balance," said one market expert at a European bank.
"The market will continue this way until there is clear direction on Fed policy," said another market source at a Wall Street investment bank.
Sources noted though that the major Latin Bradys did not suffer as much as the higher yielding instruments.
Mexican Pars were 1/2 weaker at 74-1/2 bid and its Discount bonds were 5/8 lower at 89-3/8.
As for other Latin Brady issues, Argentine Pars AR4C23=RR were 3/4 lower at 64-1/2 bid and Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/4 weaker at 76-7/8 bid.
Among Eastern European issues, Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans were one percentage point lower at 79-1/4 bid and Bulgarian IABs were unchanged at 57-1/4 bid.
